messages:
Anya: Heads-up — saw model outputs diverge after the FP8 rollout yesterday. Small but reproducible for long prompts with KV reuse. Repro steps below. Anyone seen this?
Samir: hmm, which model + kernel?
Anya: gpt-large-v2 quantized to FP8, runtime selects mixed-precision matmul path (bf16->fp8 path). Repro:
Anya: ```bash
# minimal repro
python tools/run_infer.py --model gpt-large-v2 --quant FP8 --seq 2048 --prompt tests/long_prompt.txt --reps 3
```
Anya: Logs show alternating kernel choices across batches: `matmul_kernel_v3_fp8` vs `matmul_kernel_v2_bf16_fallback`.
Leo: alternating kernel choice shouldn't happen mid-session. Is this triggered by batching heuristic or by calibration flags?
Anya: Profiler snapshot:
Anya: ```
[profile] batch_size=8 seq=2048 kv_cached=true
kernel_choice: matmul_v3_fp8 (50%) matmul_v2_bf16 (50%)
activation_scale_mean: 1.23 vs 0.98
latency_p50: 32ms vs 45ms
```
Samir: if activation scale stats diverge, calibration might change quantization path. Do we re-calibrate per-route or per-batch?
Devon: infra-bot report: `deploy 17654 to prod` around 10:42 — could be runtime flag changed.
InfraBot: Deploybot: rolled out runtime-2.14.3 -> web nodes at 1765552000
Maria: I can repro locally with a fixed seed; outputs diverge after the second batch. Could be KV cache packer alignment changing fringe values and causing different quant scales.
Samir: Can you paste a tiny diff of logits or token probs? even 1e-3 shift matters.
Maria: ```
seed=42
step1 logits[10:15]: [-0.23, 1.12, 0.04, 0.05, -0.1]
step2 logits[10:15]: [-0.25, 1.10, 0.05, 0.03, -0.12]
```
Leo: That matches scale clipping noise in the FP8 quant path. Are we zeroing small exps differently? check `quant_clip_threshold` toggle.
Anya: Found selector rule: if avg_seq_len > 1024 and batch > 4 pick `matmul_v3_fp8` else fallback. Because of dynamic batch merging some batches hover around threshold.
Samir: So batching heuristics causing non-determinism -> toggles kernel mid-inference -> different rounding. Bad for correctness.
Devon: Quick patch idea: pin kernel at session start based on expected seq_len + KV flag. If KV state changes, allow a controlled re-quant with deterministic margin.
Maria: I tested pin: `runtime.kernel_pin=true` -> outputs stable and match bf16 baseline within 1e-4.
Anya: Excellent. Need canary + perf eval: does pinning hurt throughput for typical workloads?
Leo: microbenchmarks: pin-to-bf16 +8% latency; pin-to-fp8-v3 -6% latency. Stability matters more for correctness.
Samir: Add calibration hysteresis: require 3 consecutive batches beyond threshold before switching kernels.
Devon: I'll add a quick patch to batching rules and default `kernel_pin=false` but `hysteresis=3`. Opening PR now.
Devon: PR: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/3847
Anya: Patch plan: 1) Merge hysteresis + kernel_pin opt 2) Canary to small % traffic 3) Run regression evals (eval suite + curated prompts) 4) Roll forward.
Maria: Also add a unit test that simulates dynamic batch merges and ensures stable kernel per-session.
Samir: Add note to release: potential correctness issue when dynamic batch merges cross quant thresholds.
Anya: I'll start regression job and add failing example to bugdb.
InfraBot: Canary deploy started: runtime-2.14.4-canary -> 5% traffic
Leo: ping when canary finishes, I want profiler dump.
Anya: will post results in this thread.
Devon: Update: PR merged to canary. Ran 2 reg jobs, both passed.
Anya: Canary passed on 5% after 6 hours. No divergence detected on curated set. Scheduling full rollout tomorrow.
Samir: Good. Follow-up: revisit kernel selection unit tests for calibration edge cases and add telemetry to detect mid-session kernel flips.
Maria: logged telemetry item -> TICKET-3321
Anya: Closing loop, will link perf dashboards and add a short postmortem note. :white_check_mark:
